title: Scenario: Barreling the Seven of Hearts

lines.text: Chapter eight, section three. Scenario, barreling the seven of hearts.
Suppose the turn is the seven of hearts, a card that seems neutral but actually shifts the balance toward the caller.
Her range on the flop was heavy with medium pairs and low overcards, and the seven pairs some of those medium pairs into two pair or gives new hands like nine-seven and eight-seven picked-up equity.
Your range does not gain much, because you were not calling with hands that connect with the seven.

The correct adjustment is to barrel less often but more polarized: your best value hands, the ones that welcome a big pot, keep firing, and your weakest bluff candidates are best turned into semi-bluffs that have real river plans, like backdoor flush draws that would love to hit a heart.
Meanwhile, your medium-strength hands, second pair with a decent kicker for example, should mostly check for pot control.
As always, the key discipline is asking whether each hand you are considering barreling has a plausible river plan, and if not, whether checking gets you a better result on the turn.
